items.content_text: Compare purchases using your take-home hourly income, then download your own CSV. Total = quantity × final unit price. Work hours = total ÷ hourly income. Workdays = work hours ÷ hours per workday. Include tax in your prices. No currency conversion, payroll calculation, savings prediction or buying advice. Display rounds to two decimals; totals use unrounded values.
items.title: Purchase-to-work-time worksheet

items.content_text: List when you last did each household, car or health task and how often it repeats, then download a sheet with the next due date, days left and what is overdue. Next due = last done + interval. Month intervals keep the same day of the month and fall back to the last day when it does not exist, including leap years. Days left = next due − today. Overdue below 0 days; due soon from 0 to 7. Intervals from 1 to 3650 days, weeks or months. Dates between 1900-01-01 and 2999-12-31. Up to 30 tasks. No reminders, notifications or calendar sync; nothing leaves this page.
items.title: Maintenance next-due schedule sheet

items.content_text: List what a freelance project or small job brought in and what it cost, then download a sheet with the gross profit, margin and net per hour. Profit = income total − expense total. Margin = profit ÷ income total. Net per hour = profit ÷ hours spent. Amounts are added in whole cents, so totals never drift. Amounts from 0 to 100,000,000 with at most two decimals, up to 20 income and 20 expense rows, hours from 0.25 to 2000 in quarter-hour steps. Same currency, no exchange rates, no tax or accounting advice.
items.title: Project profit sheet

items.content_text: Type the maximum capacity from iPhone Settings and, if you have it, the cycle count, then download a sheet with the wear-per-month range and the months left before 80%, always as a range and never as a score. Wear per month = (100 − capacity) ÷ age in months, shown as a ±25% band. Months to 80% = (capacity − 80) ÷ wear, low bound from the high wear rate and high bound from the low rate. Cycles per month = cycle count ÷ age. Capacity from 60 to 100 as a whole percent, cycle count from 0 to 3000, purchase month between 2007 and 2099 and one to 240 months old, up to 10 devices. Months are YYYY-MM. Inputs stay in this tab; nothing is measured or read from your phone.
items.title: Battery wear range sheet

items.content_text: List what your household does online at the same time and how many devices do it, then download a sheet with the Mbps you need and the headroom left on your plan. Total per row = devices × per-device figure. Needed = sum of the rows. Headroom = plan − needed; under 20% of the plan is tight, below zero is not enough. Figures are added in tenths of a Mbps, so totals never drift. Plan speeds from 0.5 to 10000 Mbps with at most one decimal, 1 to 50 devices per row, up to 20 rows. Wi-Fi coverage, latency and your provider's real delivered speed are outside this sheet.
items.title: Home bandwidth sheet

items.content_text: Enter one trip budget, the days, the travelers and the costs you already know, then download a sheet with how much each person can spend per day and how it splits across food, transport, tickets and shopping. Left to spend = total budget − fixed costs. Per day = left to spend ÷ days. Per person per day = per day ÷ travelers. Each category = per day × its share. Amounts are added in whole cents; daily figures are only rounded when shown. Amounts from 0 to 100,000,000 with at most two decimals, 1 to 120 days, 1 to 20 travelers, up to 15 fixed costs, four shares that add up to exactly 100. Same currency throughout, no exchange rates, no price or booking advice.
items.title: Trip budget per day sheet

items.content_text: List the places you want to visit in one day with how long you will stay and how long it takes to reach the next one, then download a sheet with arrival and departure times and whether it all fits between your start and end. Arrive = previous leave + travel. Leave = arrive + stay. Total = all stays + all travel. Available = end − start; an end time earlier than the start counts as the next day. Over by = total − available; anything above zero is over time. Plain minute arithmetic, no time zones. Times as 24-hour HH:MM, stays from 5 to 720 minutes, travel from 0 to 600 minutes, up to 25 stops. Opening hours, real traffic, maps, routing and bookings are outside this sheet.
items.title: One-day itinerary time sheet

items.content_text: Turn messy meeting notes into a one-page outline: one headline, three to twelve key points, one next action and an optional metric, then download it as a sheet you can paste into a slide or a summary. The sheet keeps your words as they are: headline, then points in the order you typed them, then the next action, then the metric. It counts the points and trims surrounding spaces; nothing is rewritten, summarised or scored. Headline up to 80 characters, 3 to 12 points of up to 160 characters each, next action up to 160 characters, metric up to 60 characters. Every line must be single-line text. The sheet does not read files, recordings or calendars.
items.title: Meeting notes to one-page outline
